title: Rice with Stewed Beans, Puerto Rican Style

content.title: About
content.content: The traditional Puerto Rican dish “arroz con gandules” is a fragrant rice cooked together with stewed beans (usually red kidney beans), spices, tomato sauce, and sometimes pork or sausage pieces. It delivers a rich, mildly spicy flavor and the distinctive aroma of Caribbean herbs.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The dish dates back to the colonial era when Spanish settlers introduced rice and beans, which locals adapted to Caribbean tastes.
Stewed beans in Puerto Rico are often called “gandules,” from the Spanish word for pigeon peas.
Traditionally the rice is cooked in a tight‑fitting pot so it absorbs the bean broth and spices.
Many versions start with a “sofrito” – a blend of onion, garlic, sweet pepper, cilantro, and tomatoes sautéed in olive oil.
It is a staple at the San Juan Festival and a common everyday comfort food.

items.title: Rich source of complex carbohydrates
items.content: Rice provides sustained energy release, helping maintain stable blood‑sugar levels.

items.title: High plant‑based protein
items.content: Beans add a substantial amount of protein, supporting muscle repair and growth.

items.title: Fiber and digestive support
items.content: Beans contribute dietary fiber that promotes healthy digestion.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Together rice and beans supply thiamine, niacin, and folate, essential for metabolism.

items.title: Minerals: iron and magnesium
items.content: Beans are a good source of iron, while rice provides magnesium, both important for muscle and nerve function.

items.title: Legume allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to beans.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: If prepared with soy sauce or pre‑made seasoning mixes, the dish can become high in sodium.

items.title: Anti‑nutrients
items.content: Raw beans contain phytic acid, which can reduce mineral absorption; they should be fully cooked.

content.title: How to Serve
content.content: Serve hot, garnished with fresh cilantro or chopped green onions. It pairs well with fried plantains, avocado slices, mango salsa, or a simple green salad.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Cool the dish to room temperature, then store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. Reheat on the stovetop or in a microwave, adding a splash of water to restore moisture.
